html:
Kaska Dena Kayeh is the land of the Kaska Dena, an Athabaskan people of the upper Liard River basin in northern British Columbia and the southeast Yukon, around today's Watson Lake, Lower Post and Ross River.

They lived by hunting moose and caribou, trapping and fishing in the boreal forest and mountains. Their neighbours were the Tahltan to the southwest and the Tagish and Tlingit to the west. The Hudson's Bay Company built posts on the Liard from the 1820s. The Cassiar Gold Rush of the 1870s brought miners, and in 1942 the Alaska Highway cut through their land, bringing disease and settlement. The Kaska today form several First Nations and are still negotiating their land rights.
